{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Licensed Technology / Hosted FX Platform Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Licence and Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Six areas come back clean and require no redline: exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, governing law and venue, MFN, and minimum purchase commitments. The commercial architecture is genuinely usage-based (volume-band per-trade fees, rebates running in our favour, a single $2,500/month support fee for services actually provided), and New York law with exclusive New York venue matches our preferred position.

The risk is concentrated in the risk-allocation and exit provisions, and it is one-sided against us in every instance. The Agreement gives us the Licensed Technology wholly "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance remedy; it contains no Licensor indemnity at all while imposing a broad one-way indemnity on us, and Article XIII affirmatively disclaims Licensor liability for IP infringement; it caps only Licensor's liability (at one half of amounts paid) leaving us uncapped; it terminates our licences automatically on our change of control; and it gives the Licensor a unilateral option to extend the 36-month term by a further seven years with no opt-out and no pricing cap, while giving us no termination for convenience. There is no transition-assistance or data-return obligation and no vendor insurance covenant — significant on a hosted platform holding our trade, order and client data. Several of these findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook rather than merely below fallback.

We have proposed redlines on each deviation and each material gap, with fallbacks identified where a landing zone exists.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us; all "exclusive" references either make our licence non-exclusive or are unrelated boilerplate. No minimum-volume or order-routing commitment. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation | No liquidated damages, late-payment penalty, shortfall charge or early-termination fee. Article XXIII bars termination damages in both directions. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § I Certain Definitions | Restraints are internal to the licence (field of use, use restrictions on Licensor's technology); nothing prevents us operating, buying or building a competing platform. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | General Provisions | New York internal law; exclusive jurisdiction of SDNY or New York state courts with venue waiver. No arbitration provision. Matches preferred position. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | Fee schedule (volume bands) | No MFN, best-price or third-party-matching obligation on us. The only "other licensees" reference runs in our favour (Revisions release). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions | Volume bands operate solely as a discount on trades actually executed; no minimum volume, take-or-pay, shortfall or true-up. Support fee is for services provided. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Confidential Information / Non-Solicitation (Art. XXI, Effect of Termination) | Article XXI runs one way only — we must ship everything back within five days with officer certification. No Licensor obligation to return or export our data, assist migration, or certify deletion. Walk-away territory on a hosted platform. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | Warranty Disclaimer (Art. VIX) | Technology provided "AS IS"; all express and implied warranties disclaimed, including any commitment that errors or non-conformity to Documentation will be corrected. No warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy anywhere. Walk-away position. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | General Provisions § (c); Art. XX(a) | Blanket ban on our assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, while Licensor is unrestricted; plus automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our change of control absent Licensor consent. Two independent walk-away features. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | Fee/records provisions | Mutually selected CPA, records-only scope, 30-day window and Licensor-borne cost (unless >5% discrepancy) are acceptable, but there is **no frequency limit** — unlimited audits fail both preferred (once per 12 months) and fallback. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | Art. XII / Art. XIII | One-way indemnity from us to Licensor covering our exercise of the licence and our business; no Licensor indemnity at all, and Article XIII expressly disclaims Licensor liability for IP infringement claims while the disclaimer excludes non-infringement. Walk-away scenario. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | General Provisions | Only "insurance" reference is a pass-through of charges payable by us. No coverage covenant despite Licensor hosting the platform and processing our data — below fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). |
| Low | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | Art. III (with Art. VII(b), definitions 1.3, 1.6) | "Intellectual Property Rights" defined solely as rights of Licensor and "Derivative Work" captures all enhancements, so the front end and customizations we fund become Licensor-owned with only a terminable licence to us. Agreement is silent on our trade, order and client data. |
| Low | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions | Grant runs to Licensee alone, access confined to "employees of the Licensee", third-party use requires consent — Affiliates (defined but unused) and contractors excluded with no notice path. Licence also does not survive an M&A transaction. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Art. XIII (with Art. XII) | Caps only Licensor, at one half of amounts paid; our liability is uncapped and expanded by the one-way indemnity. Consequential-damages exclusion is one-way and there are no carve-outs. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | Art. X(b) (with Art. XI) | One-way non-solicit on us for the Term plus three years covering all Licensor and Affiliate personnel — two walk-away triggers (>24 months; all personnel). Advertising/unsolicited-inquiry carve-out is adequate but does not cure. |
| Low | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | Art. IV | Licensor holds a unilateral option to extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years, with no Licensee opt-out and no cap on renewal pricing. Walk-away territory; conflicts with the mutual-agreement language in sub-clauses II and III. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | Art. IV (with Arts. XIX, XX) | No Licensee convenience right in a 36-month term; all termination rights run to Licensor (breach, change of control, wind-up) other than mutual insolvency termination. Fails preferred and fallback. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following findings sit in walk-away territory under the playbook. We would not recommend signing without movement on each:

1. **Warranty (Art. VIX) — "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed.** No conformance warranty and no repair/replace/refund remedy; the "commercially reasonable efforts" Error Correction/Revisions covenant is not a warranty and carries no remedy. *Fallback available:* 90-day/30-day warranty periods.
2. **Indemnification (Arts. XII and XIII) — no Licensor IP indemnity plus a one-way Customer indemnity for the Vendor's own technology,** compounded by an express disclaimer of Licensor liability for infringement claims. *Fallback available:* usual IP exclusions with procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x fees super-cap.
3. **Limitation of liability (Art. XIII) — we are uncapped while the Licensor is capped at one half of amounts paid,** with a one-way consequential-damages exclusion and no carve-outs. *Fallback available:* mutual 12-month fee cap with indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct carve-outs.
4. **Assignment and change of control (Gen. Prov. § (c); Art. XX(a)) — blanket one-sided assignment ban plus automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences on our change of control,** with Licensor deemed reasonable in withholding consent where the acquirer competes or where it merely believes its interests are affected. Note the related Article XXII right of first refusal over a sale of substantially all our assets or a merger, which further constrains our exit.
5. **Renewal (Art. IV) — unilateral seven-year Licensor extension option with no opt-out and no pricing cap.**
6. **Termination for convenience (Art. IV) — no Licensee exit right across a 36-month term.**
7. **Transition and data return (Art. XXI) — no data export, migration assistance or deletion certification,** leaving our data stranded in Licensor's systems on a hosted FX platform. *Fallback available:* 90 days' assistance with a 30-day export.

---

## Next steps

1. **Send the redline** covering the proposed edits already prepared: express warranty package with repair/replace/refund carved out of the AS IS disclaimer; Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with our indemnity narrowed to Licensee-provided content and our own breach of law; mutual liability cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 with Excluded Claims carve-outs; affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, mutual reasonable-consent standard and removal of change-of-control termination; automatic 12-month renewals with a 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder and CPI/3% uplift cap; Licensee termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with prepaid-fee refund; new Article XXI(c) transition assistance and data return; vendor insurance covenant in General Provisions; Licensee Data ownership plus ownership and licence-back of customization deliverables in Article III; extension of the licence to Affiliates and contractors with a successor-transfer right; audit frequency cap at once per 12 months with business-hours timing, auditor confidentiality and no system access; and a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in performance.
2. **Prioritise the negotiation** around the seven walk-away items, taking warranty, indemnity and liability as a single risk-allocation package rather than three separate asks — they interlock, since the Article XIII exclusions would otherwise render any indemnity illusory.
3. **Flag the fallbacks in the covering comments** where identified above, so the Licensor sees the landing zone on first pass.
4. **Confirm the business position** on (i) the Article XXII right of first refusal over a sale or merger of our business, given its interaction with the change-of-control provisions, and (ii) the value of the customizations and front-end work we expect to fund, which drives how hard we press on Article III ownership.
5. **Confirm with the business** what trade, order and client data will reside on the hosted platform, to size the transition, data-return and insurance asks.

*Note on verification status:* the findings for transition, warranty, assignment, audit, IP, licence scope and non-solicitation are recorded as verification failures, and indemnification, liability cap, renewal and termination for convenience as repaired. We should re-run verification on the redline before it goes out.
"}
